column1: # Per-sample/per-vector path-aware EDP -- SD/TC-PM and SD/TC-PPM adders.
# SD_a/SD_b together are a REDUNDANT dual-rail signed-digit encoding of ONE operand
# (digit i = SD_a(i) - SD_b(i) in {-1,0,+1}), structurally identical to TER's A_a/A_b.
# TC is a separate plain two's-complement operand.
# Monte Carlo table: matches the ORIGINAL Monte Carlo methodology exactly -- SD_a, SD_b,
# and TC each drawn independently and uniformly at random (1,000,000 samples, seed=42).
# Now covers the full 2-64-bit range. AvgSwitches verified to match the pre-existing
# monte_carlo_results.csv exactly at every width. Fixed a real truncation bug while
# extending to 32/64-bit: Sum_a/Sum_b are N+1 bits wide (33 at N=32, 65 at N=64), which
# don't fit in unsigned int/unsigned long long respectively -- now uses unsigned long
# long at 32-bit and __uint128_t at 64-bit, matching the original source's own types.
# Exhaustive table: 2^N x 2^N sweep (SD value x TC value), matching TER-BIN's 'dropped NAF'
# approach -- SD_a = the value's own bits, SD_b = 0 always (never uses the -1 digit
# state), instead of exhaustively covering all 2^(3N) (SD_a, SD_b, TC) combinations.
# warm-start fork (same technique as RCA/CLA/TER -- each worker takes a contiguous
# SD-value slice, first silently replaying the true predecessor vector (sd_start-1,
# max_TC) to reach the exact circuit state a continuous process would have reached,
# before counting). Verified byte-exact against the single-process reference at 8-bit
# before being trusted for 12/16-bit. 32/64-bit not yet built.
